title: जलवायु परिवर्तनको असरसँग जुध्न ‘रिचार्ज काठमाडौं अभियान’ सुरू
content:
No ads found for this position काठमाडौं । काठमाडौं महानगरपालिकाले ‘काठमाडौं जलवायु कार्य सप्ताह’ को उद्घाटनका अवसर पारेर आजै राष्ट्रिय सभागृहबाट ‘रिचार्ज काठमाडौं अभियान’ को सुरुआत गरेको छ। कार्यवाहक प्रधानमन्त्री विराजभक्त श्रेष्ठ, बागमती प्रदेशका मुख्यमन्त्री किरण थापा र काठमाडौं महानगरपालिकाकी कार्यवाहक मेयर सुनिता डंगोलले संयुक्त रूपमा अभियानको थालनी गरेका हुन् । अभियानको संयुक्त उद्घाटन गर्दै कार्यवाहक प्रधानमन्त्री श्रेष्ठ र मुख्यमन्त्री थापाले स्थानीय तहको पहलमा सुरु भएको यो प्रयास प्रशंसनीय रहेको बताउँदै सङ्घीय र प्रदेश सरकारको तर्फबाट पनि सकारात्मक सहयोग रहने प्रतिबद्धता व्यक्त गरे। सो अवसरमा कार्यवाहक मेयर डंगोलले अब पनि ‘गरौँला-हेरौँला’ भनेर बस्ने समय नभएको बताउँदै काममै उत्रिनुपर्छ भन्ने सन्देश दिन कार्य सप्ताह आयोजना गरिएको स्पष्ट पारिन्। महानगरपालिकाभरिका विद्यालयहरूमा कहाँ-कहाँ पानी रिचार्ज गर्न सकिन्छ भन्नेबारे अध्ययन भइसकेकाले सोहीअनुसार कार्यक्रम अघि बढाउने प्रतिबद्धता उनले व्यक्त गरिन्। उद्घाटन समारोहलाई सम्बोधन गर्दै उनले काठमाडौं महानगरपालिकाको कार्यवाहक मेयरको हैसियतमा मात्र नभई साझा पृथ्वीको एक नागरिकको हैसियतमा यो अभियानलाई कार्यान्वयनमा लैजाने अठोट जनाइन्। जलवायु परिवर्तनको असरबाट उत्पन्न विपद् र त्यसबाट भएको क्षतिमा महानगरपालिकाले विगतमा सक्दो सहयोग गरेको स्मरण गर्दै उनले सबै मिलेर क्षति न्यूनीकरणका प्रयास थाल्नुको विकल्प नरहेको उल्लेख गरिन् । कार्यक्रममा भोटेकोशी बाढी प्रभावित क्षेत्र नुवाकोटको विदुर नगरपालिकाका प्रमुख, हिमाली जिल्ला मुस्ताङको घरपझोङ गाउँपालिकाका अध्यक्ष, काठमाडौं उपत्यकाका नागार्जुन, भक्तपुर, बूढानीलकण्ठ र चन्द्रागिरि नगरपालिकाका प्रमुख तथा तराईको बारास्थित निजगढ नगरपालिकाका प्रमुखलाई एकै ठाउँमा राखेर त्यहाँका बासिन्दाले भोग्नुपरेको जलवायु परिवर्तनको असरलगायत विषयमा अनुभव आदानप्रदान गरिएको छ । Kathmandu. Kathmandu Metropolitan City has launched the 'Recharge Kathmandu Campaign' from the National Assembly today, on the occasion of the inauguration of the 'Kathmandu Climate Action Week'. The campaign was jointly launched by Acting Prime Minister Biraj Bhakta Shrestha, Chief Minister of Bagmati Province Kiran Thapa, and Acting Mayor of Kathmandu Metropolitan City Sunita Dangol. Jointly inaugurating the campaign, Acting Prime Minister Shrestha and Chief Minister Thapa said that this effort, which was initiated by the local level, was commendable and expressed their commitment to positive support from the federal and provincial governments. On the occasion, Acting Mayor Dangol clarified that there is no time to sit around and say 'let's do it and see' and that the work week was organized to send a message that we should get down to work. She expressed her commitment to move forward with the program accordingly as a study has been conducted on where water can be recharged in schools across the metropolis. Addressing the inaugural ceremony, she expressed her determination to implement this campaign not only as the acting mayor of Kathmandu Metropolitan City but also as a citizen of the common earth. Recalling that the Metropolitan City has provided all possible assistance in the past in the disasters and damages caused by the effects of climate change, she stated that there is no alternative but to start efforts to reduce the damage together. The program brought together the mayor of Bidur Municipality in Nuwakot, a Bhotekoshi flood-affected area, the chairman of Gharpajhong Rural Municipality in Mustang, the mayors of Nagarjuna, Bhaktapur, Budhanilkantha and Chandragiri municipalities in the Kathmandu Valley, and the mayor of Nijgadh Municipality in Bara in the Terai to share experiences on the impacts of climate change faced by the residents there.

Kathmandu Metropolitan City has launched the 'Recharge Kathmandu Campaign' from the National Assembly today, on the occasion of the inauguration of the 'Kathmandu Climate Action Week'. Kathmandu. Kathmandu Metropolitan City has launched the 'Recharge Kathmandu Campaign' from the National Assembly today, on the occasion of the inauguration of the 'Kathmandu Climate Action Week'. The campaign was jointly launched by Acting Prime Minister Biraj Bhakta Shrestha, Chief Minister of Bagmati Province Kiran Thapa, and Acting Mayor of Kathmandu Metropolitan City Sunita Dangol. Jointly inaugurating the campaign, Acting Prime Minister Shrestha and Chief Minister Thapa said that this effort, which was initiated by the local level, was commendable and expressed their commitment to positive support from the federal and provincial governments. On the occasion, Acting Mayor Dangol clarified that there is no time to sit around and say 'let's do it and see' and that the work week was organized to send a message that we should get down to work. She expressed her commitment to move forward with the program accordingly as a study has been conducted on where water can be recharged in schools across the metropolis. Addressing the inaugural ceremony, she expressed her determination to implement this campaign not only as the acting mayor of Kathmandu Metropolitan City but also as a citizen of the common earth. Recalling that the Metropolitan City has provided all possible assistance in the past in the disasters and damages caused by the effects of climate change, she stated that there is no alternative but to start efforts to reduce the damage together. The program brought together the mayor of Bidur Municipality in Nuwakot, a Bhotekoshi flood-affected area, the chairman of Gharpajhong Rural Municipality in Mustang, the mayors of Nagarjuna, Bhaktapur, Budhanilkantha and Chandragiri municipalities in the Kathmandu Valley, and the mayor of Nijgadh Municipality in Bara in the Terai to share experiences on the impacts of climate change faced by the residents there.
